processed_items.name: Identity-Proofed Access Control System for AI (IPACS-AI) — Zero-Trust Middleware Framework for AI-Assisted Development
processed_items.focal_document: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)

retrieval_attempts.mapping_summary:
AI stays open. Anonymity for malicious use ends.

Every component of this framework - FIDO2 hardware attestation, the middleware layer, direct memory injection, and the WORM immutable audit trail - exists to enforce one guarantee: legitimate developers lose nothing, malicious actors lose anonymity.

This Informative Reference maps the Identity-Proofed Access Control System for AI (IPACS-AI) - a zero-trust middleware framework for AI coding tools-to the NIST AI RMF 1.0. IPACS-AI closes the accountability gap created by anonymous AI access through identity-proofed, hardware-attested, time-bounded session controls. It eliminates clipboard code smuggling via direct memory injection, classifies AI-generated code risk via AST parsing, and maintains an immutable WORM hash-chained audit trail at zero per-transaction cost using local FIDO2/TPM 2.0 attestation and OIDC/SAML 2.0 federated identity. The crosswalk shows strong or exact alignment across all four AI RMF functions.
retrieval_attempts.mapping_comment: IPACS-AI is an independent, open-source framework submission. All 72 AI RMF 1.0 subcategories are addressed in the crosswalk. Documented gaps (DEI team documentation, formal TEVV testing) are transparently disclosed with planned remediation through a mandatory independent security audit prior to production deployment. The framework is licensed MIT/Apache 2.0 with no commercial restrictions. Local FIDO2/TPM attestation enables zero per-transaction cost and full offline resilience. Scope is explicitly bounded to API-connected AI services; fully air-gapped local inference is acknowledged as out of scope.

retrieval_attempts.mapping_summary: Concept Crosswalk mapping the SDOS Runtime Governance Framework — Control Catalog and Reference Document (v1.7) to the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0. SDOS is a runtime governance framework that enforces structured policy controls over AI agent operations at dispatch time, providing a structural enforcement layer independent of the underlying model's internal alignment or safety tuning. The framework binds model selection, tool invocation, outbound execution, and audit logging to governance rules through 24 controls across 9 governance domains. This Informative Reference identifies, for each mapped CSF 2.0 subcategory, the SDOS control(s) that support the subcategory's intent at the dispatch and enforcement layer.
retrieval_attempts.mapping_comment: Relationship type: Supportive. The SDOS framework operates at the dispatch and enforcement layer below model alignment, providing structural controls that support CSF 2.0 subcategory intent without claiming equivalence. 76 of 106 subcategories across GV, ID, PR, DE, RS, and RC are mapped; subcategories outside the runtime AI governance scope (e.g., physical security, personnel training, public communications, supplier contract lifecycle, hardware lifecycle) are intentionally not mapped. The Strength of Relationship column is left blank for all 17 rows where the relationship is "intersects with"; the nature of those relationships is noted in the per-row Comments column. Remaining mappings also leave the optional Strength column blank, consistent with the SDOS-to-AI-RMF-1.0 reference (v1.8) accepted into the NIST OLIR Catalog.

retrieval_attempts.mapping_summary: This informative reference maps the recommendations and guidance in NIST SP 800-81 Revision 3, Secure Domain Name System (DNS) Deployment Guide, to the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0. The mapping uses a supportive relationship style to show how SP 800-81r3 guidance supports the achievement of CSF 2.0 outcomes. SP 800-81r3 describes the different roles of DNS and provides recommendations for protecting the integrity, availability, and confidentiality of DNS services, including protective DNS, DNS protocol security (DNSSEC, encrypted DNS), and DNS infrastructure resilience. This OLIR enables organizations to understand how DNS security practices align with and support broader cybersecurity risk management objectives expressed in the CSF.
retrieval_attempts.mapping_comment: This OLIR uses a supportive relationship mapping style. SP 800-81r3 is the first revision of the Secure DNS Deployment Guide since 2013 and introduces guidance on protective DNS, encrypted DNS (DoT/DoH), DNS support for zero trust architecture, and OT/IoT DNS considerations. The mapping covers recommendations across all three pillars of the document: Protective DNS, Protecting the DNS Protocol, and Protecting DNS Services and Infrastructure.

retrieval_attempts.mapping_summary: This OLIR establishes an initial mapping between ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) version 2.0. It provides a foundation for aligning the international information security standard with the CSF’s functions, categories, and subcategories. The mapping is intended to evolve over time, supporting organisations that use both frameworks to improve their cybersecurity posture. It also encourages collaboration and discussion within the security community on how best to integrate and apply both standards in practice.
retrieval_attempts.mapping_comment: The intent of this OLIR is to initiate the formalization of the relationships between ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) version 2.0. This marks a foundational step in aligning the updated international information security standard with the latest version of the CSF. The objective is to establish a baseline mapping that reflects both frameworks’ complementary strengths, while recognising that refinements and community input will be necessary over time. This OLIR aims to act as a collaborative resource for cybersecurity and risk management professionals to explore, debate, and better understand how ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and CSF v2.0 can be used together to strengthen organizational security programs.
